fields.Name: IT106 - Kev and System One Endpoint Decision Models
fields.Description: Jared Palmer's Kev decision models and the generic SystemOneDecision driver resolve from the synced metadata through AIDecisionRunner to a real HTTP request against a System One server on loopback. KV1 the System One Endpoint vendor takes an API Key with Endpoint credential; Kev-0.8B, Kev-4B, Kev-9B and Kev-27B are Active Decision models whose effective Decision limits are 255 Choice options, 10 Score levels and 8,192 state tokens (65,536 for Kev-27B); each has one Active System One Endpoint Inference Provider row naming SystemOneDecision and kev-latest, with no cost row on that vendor; Kev-4B also has an Active OpenRouter row naming OpenRouterDecision and jaredpalmer/kev-4b-20260924 with 8,192 input tokens, at a higher priority than its self-hosted row, and an active Realtime cost row at $0.042 per million input tokens with free output. KV2 ClassFactory.CreateInstance(BaseDecision, 'SystemOneDecision', credential) returns the shipped SystemOneDecision class, which reads the endpoint from an API Key with Endpoint credential's JSON and appends /v1/systemone. KV3 starts a node:http System One server on 127.0.0.1 and runs a real AIDecisionRunner.ExecuteDecision on the Default Decision prompt with override naming Kev-4B, then Kev-27B, on the System One Endpoint vendor, the credential being the JSON an API Key with Endpoint credential resolves to: the driver POSTs the System One body for a Likelihood, a Choice and a Score question to /v1/systemone, with a bearer token for Kev-4B and no Authorization header for Kev-27B's open-server credential; the answers come back mapped (Score probabilities keyed by level name and renormalised); and the MJ: AI Prompt Runs row is recorded against that model and vendor, successful, with the served input tokens and no cost. The server is stopped after KV3. KV4 Default Decision's candidates keep their order with Clef and Kev in the catalog: Jev on OpenRouter, then LLM Decision, then the power-matched fallbacks, every new model among them; with no Cloudflare or System One credential the runner selects the first of Jev and LLM Decision it has a credential for, and with a System One credential bound to Kev-27B's row Kev-27B is a credentialed candidate that still comes after both and the selection does not change; and with every decision driver but System One's made unavailable, the run fails over from Jev and LLM Decision to Kev-27B, because AIDecisionRunner treats Default Decision's FailoverStrategy, the column default SameModelDifferentVendor, as the whole candidate list (the decision drivers are the shared scripted stand-in for this check). KV5 a real API Key with Endpoint credential created through CredentialEngine, stored encrypted (the raw Values column carries the key's marker and neither the token nor the endpoint in clear), and bound to Kev-9B's System One Endpoint model-vendor row sends Authorization: Bearer <token>, not the credential's JSON, to its loopback endpoint, and the answers map. KV6 two credentials bound to the Kev-4B and Kev-27B rows send each model's call to its own loopback server and only its own. KV7 a throwaway Decision prompt bound to Kev-9B (a token with no endpoint), Clef (a real credential with a token and no account ID) and Kev-27B (a working server) fails over twice: each misconfigured candidate fails before any request (Clef sends nothing to Cloudflare) with a NoCredentials error naming SYSTEMONE_BASE_URL or CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID, and Kev-27B answers. KV8 through the runner, a System One 503 fails over, a 429 is retried once (the prompt's MaxRetries) and then fails over, and a 401 stops the failover loop with no other candidate called, Kev-4B on OpenRouter included. KV9 an override naming Kev-4B on OpenRouter builds OpenRouterDecision, which POSTs to https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions with model jaredpalmer/kev-4b-20260924 and the bearer token, maps the answers, and records OpenRouter's reported cost. KV10 a throwaway Active Decision model with a Model Developer row and an Inference Provider row (SystemOneDecision, kev-latest) on System One Endpoint, under keys that sort the Developer row first on SQL Server and on PostgreSQL, loads with the Developer row first in AIEngine.ModelVendorsByModelID (asserted as a precondition, as is that the candidate has no credential before the binding); with a real API Key with Endpoint credential bound to the Inference Provider row only, the override's candidate has a credential, the run sees it as available, the loopback server receives the bound token and the System One body, the answers map, and the run row names the model and vendor. Before the fix, BaseModelRunner read a ModelVendor binding from only the first Active row of the model and vendor, so this binding was missed. OpenRouterDecision is replaced for the whole bundle by a subclass that overrides only SendRequest and answers only when a check arms it, CloudflareDecision by one that records the URL and refuses every request, and SYSTEMONE_BASE_URL, CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID and CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS_AI_BASE_URL are unset for the bundle, so nothing leaves 127.0.0.1. Every prompt run, test prompt, test model and its model-vendor rows, credential, binding and credential audit-log row the bundle creates is deleted, children first.

ExpectedOutcomes.summary: Kev-0.8B, Kev-4B, Kev-9B and Kev-27B are usable as Decision models: their metadata resolves with the right limits, drivers and routes (Kev-4B on OpenRouter first), the SystemOneDecision driver builds through the ClassFactory, and an AIDecisionRunner call naming a Kev model on the System One Endpoint vendor reaches the configured server, maps its answers and records the run; bound credentials route each Kev row to its own server with its token, misconfigured candidates and 503s and 429s fail over while a 401 stops, Kev-4B reaches OpenRouter, Default Decision's selection is unchanged, and a credential bound to the Inference Provider row of a model that also has a Model Developer row on the same vendor is found whichever row loads first.
